advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the captured-vector parity test assert against independently-derived expected values (not the helper's own output) so it verifies correctness, not just delegation.
evidence: `expected = link_direction.canonicalize_jira_issue_links(fields)` then `assert cloud.map_remote_links(fields) == expected` and `assert dc.map_remote_links(fields) == expected`
Both backends now delegate to the same helper: `return canonicalize_jira_issue_links(remote_fields)` (jira/backend.py:323, jira_datacenter/backend.py delegation)
Oracle and system-under-test share the same code path, so a wrong canonicalization on the fixture is invisible to this test; only the separate parametrized cases pin absolute expected values.

Both production paths return the helper verbatim: jira/backend.py:323 `return canonicalize_jira_issue_links(remote_fields)` and jira_datacenter/backend.py:533 `return canonicalize_jira_issue_links(remote_fields)`

Because expected is computed by the very function under delegation, the assertion holds for ANY output the function produces — including a buggy one — so it verifies only that delegation exists, not that canonicalization is correct on the captured data.

issuelinks_map.json every link is `"name": "Blocks"` (e.g. tests/fixtures/jira/issuelinks_map.json:48, :101, :154, :205, :257, :309, :359, :411, :461, :511); no Relates, no unmapped type, no malformed entry appear.

The Relates / unmapped-keyed-fallback / malformed-without-key branches (link_direction.py:73-80) are only asserted against the standalone helper in test_canonicalize_jira_issue_links_cases, never through cloud.map_remote_links / dc.map_remote_links.
The delegation test test_backend_map_remote_links_delegates_to_core replaces the helper with a sentinel-returning fake, so it does not exercise those branches through the backend either.
advisory.finding: The parity test `test_cloud_and_dc_match_captured_vectors` computes `expected` from `link_direction.canonicalize_jira_issue_links(fields)` and asserts both backends equal it, but both backends now delegate to that exact function — so the test can only prove delegation/non-mutation, not that the canonicalization is correct on the captured fixture. If the shared helper's logic were wrong, this test would still pass.
merged_from: test_cloud_and_dc_match_captured_vectors derives its expected value from the same canonicalize_jira_issue_links that both backends delegate to, so the equality is structurally guaranteed by delegation and cannot detect a regression in the canonicalization output values on the captured vectors (convergence twin of a fail-open oracle).

No backend-level (map_remote_links delegation-path) coverage exercises the newly centralized fallback, symmetric-relation, or malformed branches on realistic data: the captured fixture used by the only backend-driving parity test contains exclusively 'Blocks' link types.
